portable_core.compiler_runtime: Declared through the exact Zig lock.

crates.fairpane-sys: Exact declarations of the public C ABI, generated from the interface schema and shipped with it.
crates.fairpane: Safe, idiomatic Rust ownership and operations over fairpane-sys and the Rust standard library.

rust_wrapper.policy: The canonical wrapper uses only first-party code, the Rust standard library, and Rust toolchain facilities. It has no third-party runtime or build dependency, no framework-specific feature, and no async runtime requirement. Regenerating declarations is a separate development operation.

rust_browser_application.policy: The browser application welcomes qualified third-party crates for user interface and application services. A committed Cargo.lock pins every crate. Every crate passes license, advisory, source, ban, and duplicate checks across every declared target configuration, including build dependencies. The application adopts the newest qualified, compatible stack, not the independently newest version of every package.
acceptable_uses: A UI framework hosts windows, routes input and IME events, bridges accessibility, and presents engine-produced frames.
A graphics library, such as wgpu, presents an engine-produced surface in the shell.
An HTTP library supplies transport that the broker authorizes.
An accessibility adapter exposes platform objects for engine-provided semantics.
A crate supplies a host service, such as asynchronous I/O, diagnostics, configuration, profile directories, clipboard transport, file dialogs, or notifications.
outside_the_exception: A crate parses, styles, lays out, shapes, paints, or scripts web content or chrome.
A crate supplies missing page-rendering behavior behind a callback.
A crate implements web-visible network semantics, such as redirect handling, cookies, caching, or CORS, which the engine applies.
A transport crate's defaults replace the engine's Fetch semantics or transform responses.
The shell reconstructs page semantics from pixels.
A crate parses URLs, computes origins, or makes a security decision that the engine or broker owns.
A crate supplies a WebView, an embedded browser engine, or a JavaScript or WebAssembly engine.
A graphics library implements the engine's WebGPU behavior, including behind a callback, without a separate owner decision.

candidates.role: GPUI is the lead interface framework. It hosts windows, input, IME delivery, AccessKit accessibility, frame presentation, and the engine-rendered chrome. GPUI Kit's installation guide names gpui-pre as the crates.io package that publishes its paired GPUI snapshot.
The shell uses only selected GPUI Kit behavior facilities, paired with their specified GPUI snapshot. GPUI Kit documented version 0.7.1 on October 9, 2026.
Tokio is a host-service runtime, not the engine's event loop or a wrapper requirement.
The pair is a transport adapter under the broker. It returns redirects unconsumed, keeps no cookie store, and transforms no response.
Tracing emits structured shell spans correlated with engine requests and frames.
Cargo-deny is a development check for licenses, advisories, and approved dependency sources. The tool for the ban and duplicate checks stays unassigned until FP-0017 selects one.
wgpu can present engine-produced surfaces in the shell. It never implements the engine's WebGPU behavior without a separate owner decision.

excluded: Any WebView or embedded browser engine

optional_language_hosts.policy: Each language-support host is optional. Its runtime dependencies belong to that host, outside the Zig engine and the canonical wrappers. A host never executes web content or chrome. No host ships a third-party JavaScript or WebAssembly engine, a renderer, or a WebView, so JavaScript and TypeScript extensions run on Fairpane's own runtime. The default browser installation carries no third-party language runtime.

required_hosts: Node 22+ or a qualified Bun runtime
Rust from its lock once task FP-0029 creates it

note: A lexical check is not proof of the final binary dependency graph. Native artifact audits remain required.
